newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Sofia exchange bureaux win forex trade from banks.
newsitem.headline: Sofia exchange bureaux win forex trade from banks.

text.p: Bulgaria's commercial banks are using private exchange bureaux to swap dollars for marks and marks for dollars as they offer more favourable rates than the central bank since Tuesday's introduction of a currency board.

On Thursday, exchange bureaux were buying dollars at 1730-1732 and selling at 1738-1745, and buying marks at 990 and selling at 995-998. Levs were in relatively short supply as savers converted their dollars under the new, stable system.

Since Tuesday, the lev has been fixed at 1,000 to the mark in the currency board system, which matches central bank foreign exchange reserves to levs in circulation with the aim of slowing inflation and instilling monetary discipline.
Dealers said apart from the banks, their main clients were individuals converting foreign currency savings into levs now the rate is fixed.
Savings in dollars and marks are not profitable because of the fixed exchange rate and Bulgarians are switching to Treasury bills or lev deposits, a change shop dealer said.
"As demand for levs is quite high our bids and asks are lower than the BNB to cut our positions in marks," said the dealer, who asked not to be named.
On the interbank market, the lev opened at 995-995.50 per mark, and 1,741-1,745 per dollar, making foreign exchange more expensive than from exchange bureaux.

Bank dealers expect the lev to trade near or firmer than the 995 levs per mark bid of the central bank in the next few months due to the traditionally larger foreign currency supply in the summer season from tourist income. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
